metadata.title: The Three Odd Primes That Defy Every Rule of Logic
metadata.description:
Three, five, seven. Three prime numbers in a row, each one exactly two steps past the last -- the tightest a run of three primes can possibly be. Twin pairs like 11 and 13 keep showing up forever, so you would expect a run of three to turn up again somewhere too. It never does. Three, five, seven is the only one there will ever be, anywhere, and the reason fits in a single line: among any three numbers spaced two apart, one is always a multiple of three. This is the story of the one prime cluster that logic forbids outright -- and why the twin primes, the prime triplets, and the quadruplets right beside it are believed to run on without end.

Chapters:
0:00 Three in a row
1:07 The search that comes up empty
2:13 The reason in one line
3:41 But the twins never stop
4:55 Which patterns are allowed
6:16 Cousins and a quadruplet
7:34 The rule behind the rule
8:52 How close we have come
10:10 Coda
